description: Fixes three defects in the native test runtime, which is now the default execution path for `gd-tools test`. First, the base-class `GdToolsTest.wait_for_signal` is typed `-> bool` but can only ever return true, while `GdToolsTestContext.wait_for_signal` has the same name and opposite semantics, so the natural guard `if not wait_for_signal(sig): fail(...)` blocks to the per-test timeout and the test reports as `timeout` rather than `failed`; the base method gains a bounded timeout that resolves on whichever of signal or timer completes first. Second, `gd_tools_test_runner.gd::_suite_timeout` is a `for` loop that returns on its first iteration, so the first test's declared timeout becomes the `before_all` and `after_all` budget and declaration order silently sets the setup allowance; it becomes the maximum across all tests, verified order-independent. Third, cancellation of the per-test timeout is maintained by hand across three mutation sites and three readers inside a 169-line method with 11 returns, so a forgotten increment leaks a timer that fires into the next test as a spurious pass or timeout; a single `_invalidate_timeout()` becomes the only mutation site, with `_begin_test_timeout` arming through it and a new `_cancel_timeout()` serving the exit paths. A fourth task collapses the duplicated invoke-and-await bodies, keeping the two shapes distinct because the three inlined sites await an already-armed timer and must not re-arm. Phases: BOUNDED SIGNAL WAIT, SUITE TIMEOUT, TOKEN CANCELLATION, INVOKE COLLAPSE. All changes are confined to two shipped GDScript files; no Python source change and no protocol or result-schema change, with one recorded behaviour exception where a test waiting on a never-arriving signal reports `false` at the wait budget instead of running to the per-test timeout.
